Noninvasive physiological monitoring technology, p hoto-plethysmography (PPG), is widely adapted in current 
personalized healthcare devices. Most of the PPG based applications have been used PPG itself, however, PPG 
could provide more sophisticated cardiovascular information by using its derivatives. In this research, we 
investigated the sampling frequency effect to the PPG and its derivatives to provide useful information for designing 
a PPG system under limited hardware capability such as a mobile platform. In the experiment, we recorded 10 kHz 
PPG form 28 participants and created down -sampled PPGs by decimating; 5,000 Hz, 2,500 Hz, 1,000 Hz, 500 Hz, 
250 Hz, 100 Hz, 50 Hz, 25 Hz, 15 Hz, 10 Hz and 5 Hz. Then, we investigated the correlation coefficient of original, 
1st and 2 nd derivative of PPG between 10 kHz -sampled PPG and down -sampled PPGs. The r esult shows that the 
original PPG has perfect correlation (R=1.000) at fs≥25 Hz, however, correlation coefficient could not reach 1.000 in 
derivatives analysis. Especially, in 2 nd derivative analysis, correlation was not found according to the sampling 
frequency changes without preprocessing .

What sampling rate would be necessary to analyze of differentiated 
photoplethysmographic waveform morphologically? 
Hangsik Shin 
Department of Biomedical Engineering, Chonnam National University, Yeosu, Korea 
hangsik.shin@jnu.ac.kr 
Abstract 
Noninvasive physiological monitoring technology, p hoto-plethysmography (PPG), is widely adapted in current 
personalized healthcare devices. Most of the PPG based applications have been used PPG itself, however, PPG 
could provide more sophisticated cardiovascular information by using its derivatives. In this research, we 
investigated the sampling frequency effect to the PPG and its derivatives to provide useful information for designing 
a PPG system under limited hardware capability such as a mobile platform. In the experiment, we recorded 10 kHz 
PPG form 28 participants and created down -sampled PPGs by decimating; 5,000 Hz, 2,500 Hz, 1,000 Hz, 500 Hz, 
250 Hz, 100 Hz, 50 Hz, 25 Hz, 15 Hz, 10 Hz and 5 Hz. Then, we investigated the correlation coefficient of original, 
1st and 2 nd derivative of PPG between 10 kHz -sampled PPG and down -sampled PPGs. The r esult shows that the 
original PPG has perfect correlation (R=1.000) at fs≥25 Hz, however, correlation coefficient could not reach 1.000 in 
derivatives analysis. Especially, in 2 nd derivative analysis, correlation was not found according to the sampling 
frequency changes without preprocessing . 
Introduction 
Photo-plethysmography (PPG) is a widely used 
physiological monitoring t echnology in measuring of 
volume changes. Mostly PPG could provide the 
information of blood volume changes according to 
the systolic and diastolic activity of the heart. From 
these changes, we could observe the pulse wave and 
then the pulse rate could be calculated. Not only PPG 
is useful in measu ring pulse rate, but PPG could be 
investigated for assessing vascular characteristic such 
as arterial compliance or stiffness by using 1 st or 2nd 
derivatives of PPG waveform [1-3]. 
The usage of PPG has been gradually increased in 
recent personalized healthcare paradigm because 
though PPG sensing system is a low cost, easy to 
implement and non-invasive, it contains very 
important cardiovascular information. Nowadays, 
PPG is widely ada pted to the mobile healthcare 
devices and applications . For example, numerous 
wrist band type wearable devices such a s Fitbit, 
Jawbone, Samsung Gear and Applewatch as well as 
the smartphone applications for heartbeat monitoring 
are based on PPG measurement. The common 
characteristic of these system s is that the system 
resources such as the battery capacity or 
computational power are strictly limited. Therefore, 
more efficient analysis of the signal characteristic 
should be investigated. 
In this regard, o ptimization of the sampling 
frequency has been researched as a method for 
improving the efficiency of the mobile PPG system. 
In previous research , minimum requirement of 
sampling frequency has investigated fo r preserving 
morphology of PPG and for pulse rate variability 
(PRV) analysis [4-8]. These research es show that 
about 20 Hz or 25 Hz of the sampling frequency is 
required in analyzing PPG with statistical 
significance. As a next step, in this research, we 
investigate the sampling frequency effect to t he 
differentiated PPG waveform, which could be used 
for more advanced PPG -based cardiovascular 
assessment. 
Dataset 
We obtained PPG from 28 volunteers (20 males, 8 
females, age 22.0±2.9 years, height 170.2±7.3 cm, 
and weight 70.5±15.4 kg). Every data was recorded 
for 20 minutes with a 10 kHz sampling frequency 
during rest in the supine position. For signal 
recording, we used the MP150, ECG100C, 
OXY100E and Acknowledge 4.0 (Biopa c Systems 
Inc., Santa Barbara, CA, USA), and ECG and PPG 
were recorded simultaneously. To investigate the 
effect of sampling frequency, we generated down -
sampled PPGs by decimating 10 kHz PPG. Finally, 
we obtained 11 down -sampled PPGs: 5,000 Hz, 
2,500 Hz, 1,000 Hz, 500 Hz, 250 Hz, 100 Hz, 50 H z, 
25 Hz, 15 Hz, 10 Hz and 5 Hz, and then calculated 1 st

and 2nd derivatives with each down -sampled PPG. 
Morphological Correlation Analysis 
Sampling frequency effect on the original, 1st and 2nd 
derivatives PPG is investigated by comparing 
correlation coefficient (R) between 10 kHz -sampled 
reference PPG and of down -sampled PPGs. To 
calculate correlation coefficient, we used Matlab 
2015b (Mathworks inc., MA, USA) and its 
proprietary function corrcoef. 
Result and Discussion 
Figure 1 shows the correlation coefficient s between 
reference and down -sampled PPGs according to the 
sampling frequencies. The result shows that the 
original PPG preserve morphological characteristic 
well ( R=1.000) at fs≥25 Hz . However, correlation 
coefficients were drastically decreased in PPG 
derivatives and it was not reached to the R=1.000 
even though sampling frequency is increased. 
Especially, in 2 nd derivative correlation coefficient 
was very low and it means the morphology of PPG is 
severely deformed. Table 1 represents values of the 
correlation coefficient. 
These results could be explained with the 
characteristic of derivatives. General differential 
equation of discrete system is shown in (1) , and (2) is 
the frequency response on z-domain.

Figure 1 . Correlation coefficient between 1 kHz 
sampled PPG and down -sampled PPG of original, 1 st 
derivative and 2nd derivative.

From the equation (1) and (2), frequency response 
could be drawn like Figure 2, which is a kind of 
linear phase high -pass filter. This means that the 
differentiation works like a high -pass filter and this 
operation will reduce low frequency power of PPG. 
Considering that m ost of the power of PPG is 
concentrated in the low frequency range under 10 Hz 
(see. Figure 3) , d ifferentiation could remove the 
important part of PPG waveform, and it will be more 
severe by repetition. 
Figure 3 is example s of the power spectrum of 
original, 1 st derivative and 2 nd derivative. This result 
corresponds to our consideration. In Figure 3 , power 
spectrum of the original signal is relatively high er in 
low frequency band than in the high frequency band . 
However, low frequency power is decreased 
according to the differentiation. It means the loss of 
primary morphology of PPG because the essential 
energy which is closely related to PPG waveform is 
normally concentrated under around 10 Hz. In other 
words, this means that the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) 
is decreased by differentiation. Therefore, PPG signal 
will be veiled by noise and the correlation coefficient 
dramatically decrease. 
This result suggests some viewpoints ; the sampling 
frequency selection for PPG derivative ana lysis and 
preprocessing for improving SNR. In 1 st derivative 
analysis, the correlation coefficient was improved up 
to a certain level by increasing sampling frequency. 
However, in 2 nd derivative analysis, the correlation 
coefficient was not related to the sampling frequency. 
This result could be interpreted in terms of SNR. In 
case of 2 nd derivative analysis, the power of the core 
frequency band of PPG (<10 Hz) was severely 
attenuated compared with non -signal frequency band, 
and it seriously dropped the SNR. Frequency filtering 
in pre processing stage could be a good solution for 
this phenomenon. By decreasing the non -signal 
frequency range, critical degrade of SNR could be 
prevented. 
Conclusion 
In this research, we investigate d the effect of 
sampling frequency to the original, 1 st and 2 nd 
derivatives of PPG analysis. The result of this 
research suggests some considerations for PPG 
derivative analysis; morphological similarity is 
improved by increasing the sampling frequency; PPG 
derivative analysis should be accompanied with 
proper preprocessing stage. Therefore, derivative 
analysis of PPG should be investigated not only with 
the sampling frequency , but also with the 
preprocessing in further researches.
